clue.text: What bees do when really busy?

definitions.text: What bees do when really busy?

parts.words: What bees do when really busy?
parts.note: busy bees buzz loudly, and the idiom for getting things going briskly is built on that same droning noise

explanation.surface: A naturalist's question about the behaviour of bees at the height of their activity.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase literally describes bees humming as they work, and idiomatically means making an enterprise run busily and well.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means kept an enterprise lively and productive, and bees literally produce a drone while working hard.

clue.text: Everything considered, no one is left in ignorance

definitions.meaning: in sum, taking the whole lot into account

definitions.text: no one is left in ignorance
definitions.meaning: every single person has been informed

explanation.surface: Weighing it all up, a manager concludes that everybody has now been briefed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'in total' as a summing-up, and literally says every person has been informed.

clue.text: Bird droppings?

parts.note: read not as guano but as the things a hen lets drop when she lays

explanation.surface: Someone asking about the mess left by birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests guano; the question mark warns that the 'droppings' are what a bird lays.
explanation.definitionFit: A laying hen deposits these from her body, so they are literally what a bird drops.

clue.text: Pelt American all round ring? That's horrid

indicators.note: the two pieces before it together surround the ring, which sits inside them

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin, a hide
O is ring-shaped, so it stands for a ring

explanation.surface: An instruction to wrap an American fur round a ring, followed by a shudder of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean extremely ugly or unpleasant.

clue.text: Uncle is out to get us, that's the heart of the matter

indicators.note: something that is out is disordered or wrong, so the letters of uncle are put out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A family feud: an uncle is coming after us, and that's the core issue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' rearranges UNCLE into NUCLE; 'to get' only links it to US.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or central part of something is called its kernel, its centre.

clue.text: He's not a striking ex ample of comradeship

definitions.text: He's not a striking ex ample of comradeship

parts.words: He's not a striking ex ample of comradeship
parts.note: a worker who refuses to join colleagues on strike, so he is literally not a striking example of solidarity

explanation.surface: A remark that some man is hardly an outstanding model of friendship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like 'remarkable' but means 'on strike': this is the strike-breaker. The space in 'ex ample' is an OCR artefact of 'example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A strike-breaker who works while colleagues are out is scorned as betraying union solidarity.

clue.text: A lot of impetus is lost turning two directions

indicators.note: what remains of impetus is turned about into a new order
the word is is lost from impetus, so those two letters drop out of it

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north

explanation.surface: Momentum fades as something swings between two directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is lost' takes IS out of IMPETUS, leaving MPETU, which 'turning' rearranges to UMPTE; then add two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial word for a great many, an indefinitely large number.

clue.text: A chain letters sent out to old language masters

indicators.note: letters sent out are dispersed, so these letters are scattered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Schoolmasters of classics receiving and forwarding a chain letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a chain letter being mailed on; 'sent out' scrambles all thirteen letters of A CHAIN LETTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers of the tongue of ancient Rome are masters of an old language.

clue.text: Not out at close of play might even win

definitions.text: Not out at close of play might even win

parts.words: Not out at close of play might even win
parts.note: a batsman still batting when the game ends was there at the end, and a contender still present at the end may take the prize

explanation.surface: A cricket observation: a batsman unbeaten at stumps might yet see his side to victory.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'not out' means a batsman has not been dismissed; 'close of play' is the end of a day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means present at the conclusion, as a batsman unbeaten at the end or a contender still in the running is.

clue.text: Declared a supporter in a possible deal

indicators.note: the supporter goes inside the rearranged deal
a possible deal is one of the arrangements the word could take, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a leg supports a table or a body

explanation.surface: Someone announces they have a backer in a deal that might happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges the letters of 'deal' to ALED, and 'in' sends the supporter inside; the 'a' before 'supporter' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserted or claimed, typically without proof, as an accusation is.

clue.text: The climber's sole aid

parts.note: not the mountaineer's only help but a spiked frame fixed to the sole of the boot for grip on ice

explanation.surface: Someone noting that a mountaineer has only one thing to help him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like 'only', but it is the underside of the boot, where this spiked device is strapped.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal plate with spikes attached to a boot sole to give grip on ice and snow.

clue.text: Club clique, we are told

definitions.meaning: a golf club with a metal head
said aloud this is 'cleek', the name of an old golf club of the metal-headed kind

explanation.surface: A remark about a club that is really just a closed social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a sound-alike: CLEEK, pronounced like 'clique', is an old golf club of exactly this metal-headed type, so it is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf club with an angled metal head; a cleek was an early club of that kind.

clue.text: Disguise the point of cricket

definitions.meaning: a false identity or front that hides the truth
... point is a fielding position on the off side, near point

explanation.surface: A question about what cricket is really for, and what it hides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like 'purpose', but cover point is a cricket fielding position, often shortened to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: A disguise is a front or false identity, and in cricket the name is short for the fielding position cover point.

clue.text: Soundly thrash, using a crop

indicators.note: soundly here signals that a word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: beet is a root crop grown in fields

explanation.surface: Giving someone a thorough thrashing with a riding crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like the adverb of 'thrash' and 'crop' like a whip, but 'Soundly' calls for a sound-alike of BEET, a crop.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash someone is to hit them repeatedly, or to defeat them heavily.

clue.text: POWs seen around end of hostility in Welsh county

indicators.note: the prisoners are placed around the letter, which sits inside them

parts.note: taken as written: prisoners of war

indicators.note: only the final letter of hostility is taken

explanation.surface: Prisoners of war being held in Wales after fighting ended.
explanation.walkthrough: POWYS is a large rural county in mid-Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Powys is a county in mid-Wales, bordering England.

clue.text: One of five 1Is unaccountable

definitions.meaning: one of the five senses, alongside sight, hearing, smell and touch
from the saying that there is no accounting for it, since preferences cannot be explained

explanation.surface: Some single item among five that defies explanation.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to the proverb 'there's no accounting for taste'. The printed '1Is' is an OCR misreading of 'it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the five senses, and the proverb says personal preference cannot be accounted for.

clue.text: Boring new diet going round America

indicators.note: a new diet is a reworked one, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A dull new diet doing the rounds in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges DIET to TEDI; 'going' only links on to O and US.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something dull and wearisome.

clue.text: Stay true

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, especially of blood

explanation.surface: A plea to someone to remain faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like 'remain' but is the verb meaning stop, as in stemming a flow of blood; the answer also has that spelling for the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stop a flow such as bleeding; as an adjective it means steadfastly loyal.

clue.text: He should be able to identify any salt compound

definitions.text: He should be able to identify

indicators.note: a compound mixes ingredients together, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A chemist who ought to be able to identify any salt compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a chemistry noun in the surface, but it is the signal to rearrange ANY SALT.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical analyst's job is to determine what a substance is made of.

clue.text: She gave patient advice on social problems

definitions.text: She gave patient advice on social problems

parts.words: She gave patient advice on social problems
parts.note: not advice given patiently but advice given to hospital patients, the old social worker attached to a hospital

explanation.surface: A tribute to a woman who listened calmly and counselled people on social troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like the adjective 'calm', but it means hospital patients. An almoner was a hospital social worker in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital almoner was a social worker who advised patients on welfare and social matters.

clue.text: Staff upset about rising Inland Revenue taxes

indicators.note: the jumbled staff go about, that is around, the other piece
the letters of staff are upset into a different order
in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: IR is the abbreviation for the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority

explanation.surface: Tax office staff are upset about higher taxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the staff to TAFFS, and 'rising' (upwards in a down entry) turns the Revenue's abbreviation to RI, which 'about' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties levied on imports or exports.

clue.text: Doesn't encourage delays

explanation.surface: Someone who discourages things by stalling them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both deters or repels someone and postpones something.

clue.text: I get two hundred in game that's played

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
CC is two hundred in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A player boasting about scoring two hundred in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played' looks like part of the game picture, but the definition is something that is played: a musical instrument, the small flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A piccolo is a small flute, an instrument one plays.

clue.text: Moira's prepared to take soldier back for folding paper

indicators.note: the rearranged name takes the other piece into itself
the letters of Moira are prepared, that is made up anew in a different order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

indicators.note: the soldier is written back to front

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A woman named Moira is ready to bring a soldier home again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges Moira to ORAMI; 'back' turns the soldier round, and 'to take' sets those turned letters inside. The possessive 's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of folding paper into shapes.

clue.text: Pot plant

definitions.meaning: the fibrous plant itself, used for rope

explanation.surface: A houseplant in a container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot plant' reads as a houseplant, but it splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the cannabis plant, the source of the drug called pot and of rope fibre.

clue.text: Drug expert

definitions.meaning: a purified, smokable form of cocaine

explanation.surface: A specialist in narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a strong form of cocaine, and as an adjective it means highly skilled, like a crack shot.

clue.text: There's good starting in an evil symptom

indicators.note: good starts off inside the other piece, so it is placed within it

parts.note: a sin is an evil act

explanation.surface: Goodness making its first appearance in something wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is an indication or token of an underlying condition.

clue.text: Up-beat game

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to flog is to beat with a whip

explanation.surface: A cheerful, optimistic sort of game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up-beat' looks like 'cheerful', but splits: 'Up' turns FLOG, a word for beat, upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a game played with clubs over a course.

clue.text: A sign of increasing significance

parts.note: the symbol that means add, signifying an increase, and also an advantage or benefit

explanation.surface: Something that portends growing importance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an omen of growing importance; literally it is the arithmetic symbol whose meaning is addition.
explanation.definitionFit: The cross-shaped symbol denotes addition, so its significance is an increase.

clue.text: Terminate telephone or other engagement

parts.note: end a phone call by hanging up, or end a betrothal by taking off the engagement band

explanation.surface: Someone ending a phone call or calling off some other appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means to hang up a phone; read literally it also suggests removing an engagement ring, ending a betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb is British for hanging up at the end of a phone call.

clue.text: Salerno a French city? Could be!

indicators.note: the letters of Salerno could be rearranged into the city, so this signals the reshuffle

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether the Italian town Salerno is actually in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Salerno is an Italian port, which lures the solver toward Italy; its letters rearrange to a city on the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: Orléans is a city on the Loire in central France, famous for Joan of Arc.

clue.text: A chair is provided for one in this office

definitions.text: A chair is provided for one in this office

parts.words: A chair is provided for one in this office
parts.note: an academic chair is the post of a senior university teacher, so this post comes with a chair

explanation.surface: A note that the occupant of this workplace gets a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chair' and 'office' look like furniture and a room, but a chair is a university professorial post and the office is that position.
explanation.definitionFit: A university professor holds a chair, the senior academic post.
